payload.stem: The first four terms $a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4$ of a geometric series are shown in the graph, where the points are joined by line segments. What is the sum of the infinite geometric series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n$?

stimulus.description: Graph of the terms a_n for n = 1 to 4, joined by line segments.

options.why: The ratio is r = a2/a1 = \frac{2}{3} and the series converges since |r| < 1, so the sum is a1/(1 - r).

payload.stem: The population $P(t)$ of a species satisfies a logistic differential equation. The graph of $P$ and the horizontal line it approaches (dashed) are shown. For what value of $P$ is the population growing fastest?

stimulus.description: Graph of the logistic population P(t) with its horizontal asymptote drawn dashed.

options.why: Reports the initial population P(0), where growth is slow.
For a logistic model dP/dt is largest when P is half the carrying capacity, which is the value of the dashed line divided by 2.
Takes one quarter of the carrying capacity.
Reports the carrying capacity K, the limiting value, instead of the population when growth is fastest.

payload.stem: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane with position $(x(t),y(t))$. The graphs of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ for $0\le t\le 8$ are shown, and each consists of line segments. During which of the following time intervals is the particle at rest?

stimulus.description: Graphs of x(t) and y(t), each consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: Only y is constant on (4, 6); x is changing, so the particle is moving horizontally.
On this interval both graphs are horizontal, so x' = 0 and y' = 0 and the speed is zero.
Only x is constant on (0, 2); y is changing, so the particle is moving vertically.
Both x and y are changing on (6, 8), so the particle is moving.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Decide when a particle with parametric position is at rest from the slopes of both position graphs
student_thinking: The particle is at rest when x' = 0 and y' = 0 at the same time
Compare the slope of the graph of x and of y on each interval
Select the interval where both slopes are zero

key_conditions.condition: speed is sqrt((x')^2 + (y')^2) and is zero only when both derivatives are zero
key_conditions.evidence: definition of speed for planar motion

verification.independent_path: numerical speed from central differences of both interpolated graphs at each interval midpoint (independent of the slope comparison)

payload.explanation_en:
The correct answer is (2,4). On this interval both graphs are horizontal, so x' = 0 and y' = 0 and the speed is zero.
(4,6) is incorrect: Only y is constant on (4, 6); x is changing, so the particle is moving horizontally.
(0,2) is incorrect: Only x is constant on (0, 2); y is changing, so the particle is moving vertically.
(6,8) is incorrect: Both x and y are changing on (6, 8), so the particle is moving.

scope_skill.notes: Labeled 9.5 (integrating vector-valued functions), but the task is identifying rest from slopes of position graphs (derivative/speed, topic 9.2/9.4). No integration is involved, so the dominant demand is not the target topic.

key_scoring.notes: (2,4) is the unique interval where both x and y are constant.

stimulus_expression.notes: Vertex data is complete and consistent with the options. Collinear vertices at t=2 for x and t=4 for y are harmless.

distractor_explanation.notes: Distractors map to distinct misconceptions (only x flat, only y flat, both moving), and the explanation covers each one.

review.summary: The item is correct and clean, with a unique key and good distractors. It fails scope because it is labeled topic 9.5 (integrating vector-valued functions) but only tests rest from the slopes of position graphs, which is a differentiation and speed topic.
